summary: SecurityInsight 3 brings two editions, safe automatic updates, and settings that finally take effect.

new.title: Two editions: Community and Pro
new.text: SecurityInsight now comes as a free Community edition and a licensed Pro edition. Pro adds cross-engine correlation, the ServiceNow connector and sending vulnerabilities to ServiceNow or a database, with managed updates.

new.title: Safe, signed updates
new.text: Updates come through a signed update channel in stages, are checked before use and restore the previous version on failure. Pro installs update and renew their licence from Invardia by themselves.

new.title: Findings never close when a source goes silent
new.text: When a data source that had data suddenly returns none, the affected reports keep their last complete result. None of their findings is closed or marked as fixed.

new.title: One daily pipeline: Collect, Correlate, Deliver
new.text: The daily jobs run as one pipeline at 22:00 in your time zone, and nothing is delivered from an incomplete collection. Run now works on the whole pipeline, a stage or a step.

new.title: Smaller improvements
new.text: The Detailed report is now the default. Also new: Defender for Cloud recommendations and vulnerabilities, a daily trend in Community, managed identity sign-in by default, report-only asset tagging, and visible version numbers.

fixes.title: Your settings now override shipped defaults
fixes.text: Settings in your own configuration now win over the shipped defaults, as documented. This affects about 60 settings.

fixes.title: Your asset rules win over the CMDB
fixes.text: When your own asset rule sets a CMDB name, criticality or data sensitivity, that value now wins over the CMDB record, field by field.

fixes.title: Reports see every vulnerability and recommendation
fixes.text: The vulnerability reports now also read Defender Vulnerability Management directly, and Azure recommendations no longer go missing. Expect these reports to grow.

fixes.title: One machine, one tier everywhere
fixes.text: A machine seen by several sources is one asset with one tier and one name in every report. Large Summary reports also keep every asset.

fixes.title: Smaller fixes
fixes.text: Trend figures now count assets, devices sharing a name are profiled separately, hosted jobs receive all your non-secret settings, Shodan included, and Risk Analysis and asset profiling are more accurate.
